- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing downward momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model reacts slowly to sentiment turning points, especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes: model often peaks too high after a spike, then corrects sharply — use smoothing or decay on recent highs.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent trends, underestimating long-term mean reversion in volatile regimes — apply decay factor to recent history.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (e.g., 2024-07-23 to 2024-08-05) — adjust for baseline drift or seasonal correction.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.1, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.2, increase forecast by 5–10% to counter pessimism.
